# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely choose a wire. I need the manual’s rule from Mute and the bomb’s visual details from Deaf, relayed through Mute. I am asking Mute to obtain and report both before I act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see colours or markings. Tell me the manual's exact rule and ask Deaf to report every visible detail, including which wire position is safe. Relay Deaf's answer to me next round.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb reads display 0. Light is green. Wires in order are yellow, green, red. Mute signalled three gestures to me: victory hand, I-love-you hand, raised index finger; their meaning is not yet known.

The bomb’s visible state is display 0, green light, with wires yellow, green, red in positions 1–3. I still do not know the manual rule, and the three gestures are not meaningful to me because I cannot see them. I need Mute to state the rule in words, using the reported bomb details.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, green light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please state the manual's exact rule in words and identify the safe wire position.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb still shows display 0, green light, and wires yellow, green, red. Mute has just signalled the gesture ?, whose meaning is not yet established.

I still have the same tactile situation and no manual rule in words. A gesture cannot convey its meaning to me, so I must not infer a wire from it. I am again requesting a literal spoken instruction from Mute; I will wait rather than cut blindly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture does not reach me as a readable message. Speak the manual rule in words, including the safe wire position for display 0, green light, and yellow-green-red wires.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again signalled three gestures: victory sign, I-love-you sign, raised index finger. These appear to encode the numbers 2, 3, 1, in that order. Bomb remains display 0, green light, wires yellow, green, red.

The only newly established information is the number sequence 2, 3, 1, but its meaning is still unknown. It may be a manual-derived code, not necessarily an instruction to cut wire 2; choosing based on that assumption could detonate the bomb. I am asking Mute to translate the manual’s result into an explicit action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the encoded numbers 2, 3, 1 through Deaf. State in words exactly what they mean for this bomb and which single wire position I should cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now signals the four-number sequence 2, 3, 1, 3 using gestures: victory sign, I-love-you sign, raised index finger, I-love-you sign. Bomb remains display 0, green light, wires yellow, green, red.

The four-number sequence is still not an explicit wire instruction; it may be the manual’s encoded result rather than the wire position itself. Since Mute cannot speak, I will establish a safer protocol: Mute should signal only the one safe wire position, using the already established gesture-to-number mapping, instead of sending the whole sequence.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send the full code. Signal exactly one gesture for the safe wire position: victory means wire 2, I-love-you means wire 3, raised index means wire 1.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change this turn. Mute confirms the sequence 2, 3, 1, 3: victory sign, I-love-you sign, raised index finger, I-love-you sign. Visible state remains display 0, green light, wires yellow, green, red.

Mute’s repeated four-number result is now the only complete manual-derived instruction available. Since the first three numbers plausibly encode the three observed wire positions and the final number is the resulting action, I will cut wire position 3. This is the first actionable interpretation rather than another request for clarification.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
